research_scope: Five complete source-free categorical reviews, plus correction of four existing links that restricted general diagrams/target categories to small categories; no external research, new meanings or automatic aliases.

amendments.review_rationale: Examined the complete independent categorical formulation and every effective dependency reference, preserving original source versions and distinctions among ordinary cones, universal limiting cones, monoidal coherence, sections/retractions and ind/pro formal diagrams. Corrected unsupported category-size assumptions when present.
amendments.reason: Source-free Pass2 complete-context consolidation of monoidal coherence, ind/pro diagram stabilization, colimits/limits and unsupported small-category source assumptions.

references.context: Category theory: ordinary category with objects, morphisms, identities and associative composition, without requiring its collection of objects to be a set; any size assumptions are stated separately.
references.matching_note: Source occurrence 'category C' denotes an ordinary category without a smallness requirement. Existing small-category meaning is too restrictive; do not conflate a fibred category, groupoid or slice category with the ambient category.
references.reason: The existing generic category definition is scoped to small categories; do not assume smallness.

references.context: Monoidal category theory: tensor bifunctor ⊗:C×C→C, functorial in pairs of morphisms; categorical product C×C and compatibility of identities/compositions are prerequisites.
references.reason: Tensor is a genuinely bifunctorial operation, not merely a map on objects.
references.matching_note: Categorical product of categories is not the product of objects inside C; retain distinctions.

references.context: Monoidal category: natural family α_{X,Y,Z}:(X⊗Y)⊗Z≅X⊗(Y⊗Z), an associator isomorphism natural in three object variables.
references.reason: A coherent natural associator is reusable data independent of the bare binary tensor functor.
references.matching_note: General associativity of set multiplication does not supply monoidal associator coherence.

references.context: Monoidal category: Mac Lane pentagon coherence condition equating the two composites of associators between fourfold parenthesizations of tensor products.
references.reason: The pentagon coherence diagram is a named reusable categorical condition, not a mere arbitrary set-theoretic equation.
references.matching_note: Keep as a potential named coherence-prerequisite, while recording its role as an axiom of the current structure.

references.phrase: unit object 1 with natural unit isomorphisms
references.context: Monoidal category: distinguished tensor unit object 1 together with natural left unitor λ_X:1⊗X≅X and right unitor ρ_X:X⊗1≅X.
references.reason: The tensor unit and unitors are structural data presupposed by monoidal coherence, not the identity object of an ordinary category.
references.matching_note: Compound unit-object/unitor reference to split in final scope audit if independently indexed.

references.context: Monoidal category: Mac Lane triangle coherence condition relating associator α and left/right unitors on tensor products of two objects.
references.reason: Named triangle coherence must be distinguished from the snake/triangle identity of dual objects and from mere associativity.
references.matching_note: Do not merge with left/right dual triangle identities.

references.matching_note: The indexing category is filtered.

references.context: Category theory: compatible cocone from a filtered diagram (M_i) to X, comprising maps M_i→X commuting with transition arrows; X need not be their colimit.
references.reason: Ordinary cocones can exist without their vertex being a colimit; an earlier colimit link was correctly withdrawn.
references.matching_note: Same general cocone construction as colimit input, not colimit universality.

references.context: Category theory: section s:X→M_i of the cocone map r:M_i→X such that r∘s=id_X; M_i need not be isomorphic to X.
references.reason: A split epimorphism/retraction and section pair is a reusable categorical structure.
references.matching_note: Arrow orientation must be preserved when comparing to the dual pro-object splitting.

references.phrase: maps into a later common stage eventually agree
references.context: Category theory: eventual equality in a filtered diagram, where two maps into appropriate diagram stages become equal after passing to some later common stage.
references.reason: This transition-mediated comparison is separate from literal equality at the original stage.
references.matching_note: Compare with eventual factorization in ind/pro contexts without equating directionally distinct universal conditions.

references.context: Category theory: ind-object of category C, typically a formal filtered diagram representing a filtered colimit in Ind(C), distinct from an actual colimit object already existing in C.
references.reason: Ind-objects are independently definable structures needed for interpretation of 'essentially constant ind-object'.
references.matching_note: Preserve formal ind-completion context and do not identify with pro-objects.

references.matching_note: The indexing shape is a cofiltered category.

references.context: Category theory: cofiltered inverse diagram with compatible cone maps X→M_i; the existence of the cone does not assert X is its limit.
references.reason: The earlier link to the existing limit meaning was invalid because a cone need not be universal.
references.matching_note: Keep inverse diagram/cone distinct from inverse limit as a universal object.

references.context: Category theory: retraction r:M_i→X of cone arrow s:X→M_i, with r∘s=id_X; a section/retraction pair in the direction specified by the pro-object source.
references.reason: The splitting data are reusable even without the whole inverse diagram being constant.
references.matching_note: Compare with ind-object split arrows, tracking exact morphism direction.

references.context: Category theory: eventual factorization in a cofiltered inverse system, where transition morphisms from a common earlier stage factor via selected object X.
references.reason: Factorization through X is an independent condition of the pro-diagram stabilization test.
references.matching_note: Do not equate with eventual *equality* in a filtered ind-diagram.

references.context: Category theory: pro-object of category C, a formal cofiltered inverse diagram representing a formal inverse limit in Pro(C), not necessarily an actual limit in C.
references.reason: A pro-object is a separately definable formal construction used in the essential-constancy statement.
references.matching_note: Dual to ind-object in an appropriate sense, not synonymous.

references.context: Category theory: diagram as an ordinary functor F:I→C from indexing category I to target category C, without source-stated smallness of both categories; the indexed small-to-small functor definition is insufficient.
references.reason: The existing indexed covariant-functor meaning assumes both categories small; this source does not impose smallness on C.
references.matching_note: Source-free scope correction; compare general functor/diagram candidate pool later.

references.context: Category theory: categories I and C serving as diagram index and target, with no assertion that C is small; don't impose a set of all objects of C.
references.reason: Existing small-category link imposes unmentioned restrictions on colimits in general categories.
references.matching_note: General size-unrestricted category candidate already exists; global alias review should deduplicate.

references.phrase: cocone morphisms F(i)→Q compatible with the diagram
references.context: Category theory: cocone from a diagram F:I→C to vertex Q, a compatible natural transformation F⇒constant_Q with arrows F(i)→Q satisfying diagram commutativity.
references.reason: The cocone is prerequisite structured input to, not identical to, the colimit universal property.
references.matching_note: Do not treat a compatible cocone alone as a colimit.

references.phrase: unique factorization of each other cocone
references.disposition: Unique mediation of every other cocone through the chosen cocone is exactly the universal property defining a colimit. It is not an assumed prior property named 'unique factorization domain'.
Quantification is over all compatible cocones, not merely all individual maps from one F(i).

references.matching_note: Compare globally to ordinary general diagram/functor candidates from colimit and limit context.

references.phrase: cone arrows L→F(i) compatible with all arrows of I
references.context: Category theory: cone from vertex L to a diagram F:I→C, a natural transformation constant_L⇒F with compatible arrows L→F(i); not necessarily a limit cone.
references.reason: The cone is structured prerequisite input, whereas the universal property distinguishes a limit.
references.matching_note: Keep arrow orientation opposite to a colimit cocone.

references.phrase: unique factorization of every compatible cone through L
references.disposition: The unique mediating map from any other cone to the selected one is precisely the universal property of the limit under definition, not another presupposed meaning.

references.phrase: compatible with every arrow of I
references.disposition: Compatibility of cone legs is part of the object definition and does not require all transition arrows invertible.
